title: Board Policy 2020-05: refrigerator and freezer ranges, twice-daily review and the excursion action plan
rule_summary: Board of Registration in Pharmacy Policy 2020-05, Refrigerated and Frozen Medication Storage (adopted 6/26/20, revised 10/23/20), sets forth required conditions for storing refrigerated and frozen medications in Board-licensed pharmacies. It states that pharmacies shall, among other things: handle and store medications and vaccines according to package inserts and the latest CDC vaccine storage guidelines; assure cold chain processes are maintained at all times, including during delivery and shipping; in accordance with USP <1079>, maintain refrigerator temperatures between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C) and freezer temperatures between -13°F and 14°F (-25°C and -10°C); develop a policy and procedure for maintenance, monitoring and cleaning of the equipment and a back-up plan for a power failure or other unforeseen event; use thermometers with a certificate of calibration testing from an accredited laboratory, calibrated on the manufacturer's suggested timeline; review and document temperatures of each unit at least twice daily, with a mechanism to identify excursions on any days the pharmacy may be closed, each log identifying the unit and the reviewer and being readily retrievable upon request; not store food or beverage products in medication refrigerators or freezers; and use freezer units that are frost-free with an automatic defrost cycle, except that for highly temperature sensitive medications a freezer without an automatic defrost cycle may be used with a manual process to monitor and remove frost buildup. To address excursions it calls for a policy and procedure with an action plan including such steps as documenting the excursion, assessing its length and magnitude and quarantining products as necessary, contacting manufacturers to confirm safety and efficacy, removing from active inventory all visibly altered or damaged product (such as refrigerated product that has been frozen) and any product that cannot be confirmed safe and effective by the manufacturer, documenting confirmation of safety and effectiveness before returning product to active inventory, and notifying the patient and the patient's health care provider if an unsafe or ineffective product was administered or dispensed.
exam_relevance: Supplies the Board guidance to which 247 CMR 9.22(3) points: the numeric ranges, the twice-daily review, and the steps of an excursion response.

authority.name: Board of Registration in Pharmacy Policy 2020-05: Refrigerated and Frozen Medication Storage

numeric_facts.fact: minimum frequency of temperature review and documentation

exceptions: For highly temperature sensitive medications the policy allows a freezer unit without an automatic defrost cycle, with a manual process to monitor and remove frost buildup.
common_confusions: The ranges and the twice-daily review come from Board policy, to which 247 CMR 9.22(3) points by requiring temperatures to be measured and maintained in accordance with Board guidance; they are not written into the regulation.
Returning an excursion-affected product to active inventory follows documented confirmation of its safety and effectiveness, not the return of the unit to range.
